headline: Argentina vaults back to No. 1 in FIFA rankings ahead of World Cup
summary: The defending champions reclaim the top spot after tune-up victories over Iceland and Honduras, displacing Spain and France.
details: Defending World Cup champion Argentina has reclaimed the top spot in the FIFA Men's World Ranking, jumping two spots from No. 3 to No. 1.
The climb was fueled by tune-up victories over Iceland and Honduras just hours before the 2026 World Cup tournament is set to begin.

caption:
Argentina is back on top! 🇦🇷 The defending champions reclaim the No. 1 spot in the FIFA rankings just in time for the World Cup.

Defending World Cup champion Argentina has reclaimed the top spot in the FIFA Men's World Ranking, jumping two spots from No. 3 to No. 1.

The climb was fueled by tune-up victories over Iceland and Honduras just hours before the 2026 World Cup tournament is set to begin.

Led by Lionel Messi, Argentina will open their campaign in Group J on Tuesday in Kansas City, Missouri, against Algeria.

Spain remains in second place, while France has dropped to No. 3 after a tune-up loss to Ivory Coast.

Among the co-hosts, Mexico is the highest ranked at No. 14, while the United States is at No. 17 and Canada is at No. 30.

Other top 10 teams include England at No. 4, Portugal at No. 5, Brazil at No. 6, Morocco at No. 7, Netherlands at No. 8, Belgium at No. 9, and Germany at No. 10.

Italy, ranked No. 12, is the highest-ranked team that failed to qualify for the 2026 tournament, alongside Denmark (No. 21) and Nigeria (No. 26).

headline_marked: Japan captain Wataru Endo [[out of World Cup and retires]] from internationals
headline: Japan captain Wataru Endo out of World Cup and retires from internationals
summary: The Liverpool midfielder announced his retirement from the national team after failing to recover from a foot injury ahead of Japan's opener against the Netherlands.
details: Japan captain Wataru Endo has been ruled out of the World Cup and announced his international retirement on Thursday, just three days before the team's opening match against the Netherlands.
The 33-year-old Liverpool midfielder failed to recover from a foot injury sustained in February. He will be replaced in the squad by Borussia Monchengladbach's Shuto Machino.
Endo expressed his frustration on social media but urged fans to believe in the team's ability to win the World Cup in North America, stating he will now support Japan as a fan.
Despite returning for a friendly against Iceland in May, Endo continued to feel discomfort during the pre-World Cup camp in Mexico and was unable to reach full match fitness in Nashville.
Endo retires with 73 caps and four goals, having captained the side since the Qatar World Cup and playing a key role in historic wins over Germany and Spain.
Defender Ko Itakura will take over as captain. Japan has faced several injury blows, including the absences of Kaoru Mitoma and Takumi Minamino.
caption:
A massive blow for Japan: Captain Wataru Endo is out of the World Cup and retiring from international football.

Japan captain Wataru Endo has been ruled out of the World Cup and announced his international retirement on Thursday, just three days before the team's opening match against the Netherlands.

The 33-year-old Liverpool midfielder failed to recover from a foot injury sustained in February. He will be replaced in the squad by Borussia Monchengladbach's Shuto Machino.

Endo expressed his frustration on social media but urged fans to believe in the team's ability to win the World Cup in North America, stating he will now support Japan as a fan.

Despite returning for a friendly against Iceland in May, Endo continued to feel discomfort during the pre-World Cup camp in Mexico and was unable to reach full match fitness in Nashville.

Endo retires with 73 caps and four goals, having captained the side since the Qatar World Cup and playing a key role in historic wins over Germany and Spain.

Defender Ko Itakura will take over as captain. Japan has faced several injury blows, including the absences of Kaoru Mitoma and Takumi Minamino.
